request.spec:
The sheet has a fiscal year start month (settings, 1 to 12, 1 unless set, not dated;
SETTING_CHANGED key=fiscal-start-month value=<month>; anything else is refused). A fiscal year is
named FY<yyyy> by the calendar year its first day falls in; show on each period the fiscal year its
from-date falls in. A year entry and a button generate that fiscal year's twelve monthly periods
exactly as the period generator does; show how many were made.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has a fiscal year start month (settings, 1 to 12, 1 unless set, not dated;
SETTING_CHANGED key=fiscal-start-month value=<month>; anything else is refused). A fiscal year is
named FY<yyyy> by the calendar year its first day falls in; show on each period the fiscal year its
from-date falls in. A year entry and a button generate that fiscal year's twelve monthly periods
exactly as the period generator does; show how many were made.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The fiscal year change is in, and all 4 tests in the acceptance spec pass with `PORT=3417 bin/e2e`.

**One thing about the test run:** my first `bin/e2e` run on the default port 3000 failed all 4 tests. Something else was already listening on 3000, so our app couldn't start and the tests ran against that other server. The run on port 3417 passed.

**What changed:**

- **Stored data:** a new migration `V79__sheet_fiscal_start_month.sql` adds a `fiscal_start_month` column to the sheet, which is 1 unless set. Cloning a sheet copies the setting too.
- **Setting:** a new `PUT …/settings/fiscal-start-month` endpoint accepts only 1 to 12. Each save writes `SETTING_CHANGED … key=fiscal-start-month value=<month>` to the audit file. Anything else is refused by both the form and the server, and nothing is written.
- **Fiscal year on each period:** the server works out the fiscal year from the period's from-date and sends it with every period as `FY<yyyy>`, the calendar year in which that fiscal year's first day falls. For example, with a start month of 4, 2025-12-20 is in FY2025 and 2026-04-01 is in FY2026. It appears in a new "Fiscal year" column (`period-fy`).
- **Generate a fiscal year:** a new `POST …/periods/generate-fy` endpoint works out the twelve months of that fiscal year and passes them to the existing period generator. Months whose name is taken or that overlap an existing period are skipped in the same way, and the audit records are the same.
- **Screen:**
  - The settings form has a fiscal-start-month field and shows the value in force.
  - The periods screen has a year box (`period-generate-fy-year`) and a button (`period-generate-fy`).
  - That button reports its count in the same place as the existing generator (`period-generated`) and its errors in the same error element (`period-generate-error`), which is what the test expects. I moved both elements out of the generator's form so the two forms can share them.
